_comment: temper-orchestration's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of wasm_expected_failures.json
(temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json and wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json.
Same contract, same reasoning -- see wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why
divergences are LISTED and executed rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because
run_wasm_tests.mjs exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no
registered test. Point the runner at this one with
`--expected-failures tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_orchestration.json` when the module
carries temper-orchestration alone.
Currently empty. `pipeline::tests::*` (all 10 of the crate's `PipelineRunner` unit tests)
hit exactly this class of divergence during development -- `PipelineRunner::run()` read
`std::time::Instant::now()` unconditionally for stage-timing instrumentation, which panics
('time not implemented on this platform') on wasm32-unknown-unknown, the same class of bug
`temper-geometry`'s `bottleneck_geometry` deadline check documents and works around (see
that module's doc). Unlike that case, `PipelineRunner::run()` cannot avoid the clock read by
not being called -- it is plain generic Rust exercised directly by this crate's own
`#[cfg(test)]` unit tests, not gated behind `python` -- so the fix landed in `pipeline.rs`
itself (a `ClockPoint` type that is `std::time::Instant` on every other target and a
constant `0.0`ms reading on `wasm32`) rather than as a catalogued expected failure here.
Native behaviour (every other target) is unchanged; this is a genuine wasm32 platform
divergence closed at the source, in the same spirit as the `#941`/`#946` clock-bug fixes
this catalogue's sibling files reference.
Native baseline, for contrast: `cargo test --manifest-path packages/temper-orchestration/Cargo.toml`
passes 141/141 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
